[[TASK-DEFINITION]] You will be given a worked example. Your job is to translate the [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] according to the [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]]. [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] [[PROGRAM-NAME]] Calculating the Winning Percentage of a Sports Team (Case 1) [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]] Construct a program that receives from the user the number of games that a sports team won in a tournament of 12 games and calculates the winning percentage of that sports team. The program must ask for the number of the games won until the user enters a valid number. [[SOURCE-CODE]] [[LINE01]] #Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables which we need for this program [[LINE02]] total_games = 12 [[LINE03]] #Step 2: Read the number that the user enters [[LINE04]] text = input("Enter the number of games that the sports team won in the tournament: ") [[LINE05]] wins = int(text) [[LINE06]] #Step 3: Validate the user input, ask for a valid input as long as the user enters an invalid number; otherwise stop [[LINE07]] while wins < 0 or wins > total_games : [[LINE08]] text = input("Enter the number of games that the sports team won in the tournament: ") [[LINE09]] wins = int(text) [[LINE10]] #Step 4: Calculate and print the percentage of games won by a team [[LINE11]] ratio = wins / total_games [[LINE12]] print("Winning percentage:", ratio) [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]] [[LINE02.EXPL1]] We need variable total_games to store the total number of games in the tournament. This is required for calculating the percentage of the games that the sports team won. We initialize it to 12 because we have 12 games in the tournament. [[LINE04.EXPL1]] We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the number of games that the sports team won in the tournament, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string. [[LINE05.EXPL1]] We need to convert the input text to its integer representation. For this purpose, we use the conversion function int(). [[LINE05.EXPL2]] Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer. [[LINE07.EXPL1]] We need to validate the number that the user has entered and ask for a valid input as long as the user enters an invalid number. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the number that the user entered is an invalid number.

The input is an invalid number if it is outside the valid range, that is when the number that the user enters is negative or greater than the total number of games in the tournament. [[LINE07.EXPL2]] The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user enters an integer that is negative (less than zero) or greater than the total number of games in the tournament. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to False, that is when the user enters a non-negative number that is less than or equal to the total number of games in the tournament.

Note that the logical or operator is True if one or the other or both operands are True. [[LINE08.EXPL1]] We prompt the user to enter the number of games that the sports team won because the previous number was not a valid number. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function.

This statement prompts the user to enter the number of games that the sports team won in the tournament, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string. [[LINE09.EXPL1]] We need to convert the input text to its integer representation. For this purpose, we use the conversion function int(). [[LINE09.EXPL2]] Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer. [[LINE11.EXPL1]] We need to calculate the percentage of game that the sports team won by dividing the number of games won by the total number of games in the tournament. We store the result of the division into variable ratio.

Note that since we want to keep the fractional part of the division result, we need to use the real division by using / operator. [[LINE12.EXPL1]] This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Winning percentage:" and the value of variable ratio.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end. [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]] [[DIST1.LC]] while wins < 0 and wins > total_games : [[DIST2.LC]] while wins > 0 and wins <= total_games : [[DIST3.LC]] while wins > 0 or wins <= total_games : [[DIST4.LC]] ratio = wins // total_games [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]] Translate the given worked example into Arabic. Be sure to specifically translate the sections labeled [[PROGRAM-NAME]], [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]], [[SOURCE-CODE]], [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]], and [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]]. In the [[SOURCE-CODE]] section, translate ONLY user-defined string-literals and comments; make sure they are ASCII-folded (i.e., remove any accents or non-ASCII characters). Preserve the original format and Do NOT add, remove, or change any content beyond translation.
